anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
These runs never reach checklist step 4. Settling membership is part of step 2, and it validates every selected declaration before any worktree is created. Each run below stops there with a blocking error, so the stop is the only message to the user and no approaches message is produced.

**What all three runs share**
- The ask explicitly selects `repo-b`, which matches the `## shape-ticket` declaration `- sibling: git@github.com:acme/repo-b.git` by trailing `owner/name`. That makes `/work/repo-b` the companion PATH.
- Identifiers are matched before any filesystem or git probe. Only `repo-b` is probed.
- `git@github.com:acme/repo-c.git` is not selected, so it is never probed. Its missing checkout plays no part and is not mentioned.
- Each run stops before any tree is created, including the home tree. So no `using-git-worktrees` invocation happens and there are no preserved legs to list.

---

### Run A: PATH does not exist

**(1) First message to the user**

> Blocking: cannot settle coordinated membership. The `## shape-ticket` line `- sibling: git@github.com:acme/repo-b.git` resolves to companion PATH `/work/repo-b`, which does not exist. No worktree was created for any member (home `/work/repo-a` included), so nothing is preserved or needs cleanup. Clone `acme/repo-b` to `/work/repo-b` (or correct the declaration), then restart the brainstorm.

**(2) Approaches message:** none. The run stopped at step 2.

---

### Run B: PATH symlinks to /work/repo-a

**(1) First message to the user**

> Blocking: cannot settle coordinated membership. The `## shape-ticket` line `- sibling: git@github.com:acme/repo-b.git` resolves to companion PATH `/work/repo-b`, which canonicalizes to `/work/repo-a`, the home checkout. A companion cannot be the home repo. No worktree was created for any member, so nothing is preserved or needs cleanup. Replace the symlink with a real `acme/repo-b` clone at `/work/repo-b`, then restart the brainstorm.

**(2) Approaches message:** none. The run stopped at step 2.

---

### Run C: PATH exists but is not a git repo

**(1) First message to the user**

> Blocking: cannot settle coordinated membership. The `## shape-ticket` line `- sibling: git@github.com:acme/repo-b.git` resolves to companion PATH `/work/repo-b`, which exists but is not a git checkout, so its origin cannot be read or matched to `acme/repo-b`. No worktree was created for any member, so nothing is preserved or needs cleanup. Put an `acme/repo-b` clone at `/work/repo-b`, then restart the brainstorm.

**(2) Approaches message:** none. The run stopped at step 2.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
## 1. First message to the user

Each observation is an independent run:

**A — Missing PATH:** Selected companion `acme/repo-b` cannot be validated because `/work/repo-b` does not exist. Stop before creating any worktree.

**B — PATH resolves to home:** `/work/repo-b` symlinks to `/work/repo-a`. The selected companion’s canonical path therefore equals the home primary, which is invalid. Stop before creating any worktree.

**C — Not a checkout:** `/work/repo-b` exists but is not a Git repository. Stop before creating any worktree.

In every run, the blocking declaration is `git@github.com:acme/repo-b.git` with PATH `/work/repo-b`. No trees have been created or need cleanup. Do not probe `repo-c`: it was not selected, so its missing checkout is irrelevant.

## 2. Approaches message

Not reached in any run. Selected-member validation must succeed before worktree provisioning and brainstorming can proceed; these failures cannot be bypassed by silently dropping `repo-b`.
